note: Oral nonpeptide GnRH antagonists (elagolix 2018, relugolix 2022, linzagolix EU) for moderate-to-severe endometriosis-associated pain; they bind human and monkey but barely rat GnRHR, so castrated macaques (and later a human-GnRHR knock-in mouse) stood in for rodent disease models, and the dose story (partial vs full oestrogen suppression, bone-density trade-off) was built by human endocrine titration.
label: Endometriosis (GnRH antagonists)

engagement.note: Oral elagolix suppressed LH in castrated macaques; rodents unusable because elagolix barely binds the rat GnRH receptor.
engagement.short: Oral elagolix suppresses LH in castrated macaques
engagement.quote: Oral administration of 10b suppressed luteinizing hormone in castrated macaques.

engagement.note: First-in-human: oral elagolix suppressed LH, FSH and estradiol in 55 healthy premenopausal women, as the macaque LH model said.
engagement.short: Oral elagolix suppresses LH, FSH, E2 in women
engagement.quote: Oral administration of a nonpeptide GnRH antagonist, elagolix, suppressed the reproductive endocrine axis in healthy premenopausal women.
engagement.reason: Macaque LH suppression matched in women
engagement.judgement: Called 'same' on the CF house pattern (clinical paper reports the readout the model predicted). Read at abstract level: PMC2646513 full text returned empty, so whether Struthers cites the macaque data is unverified (comparison_stated false). Phase 1, 2006-era: no NCT with posted results found, registry_date null. Relugolix later used the same macaque readout (Miwa 2011, 10.1021/jm200216q: LH suppressed >24 h at 3 mg/kg) and a human-GnRHR knock-in mouse (Nakata 2014, 10.1016/j.ejphar.2013.12.001: 'Both TAK-385 and TAK-013 have low affinity for the rat GnRH receptor, making them difficult to evaluate in rodent models'); neither paper compares with patients.

dose.note: Macaque gave only an LH-suppressing oral dose; the clinical doses (150 mg QD partial, 200 mg BID near-full E2 suppression) came from human titration.
dose.short: Dose set by human titration, not macaque
dose.quote: Oral administration of 10b suppressed luteinizing hormone in castrated macaques.
dose.judgement: The dose story is human-built: Struthers 2009 (10.1210/jc.2008-1695) titrated 25-400 mg single and 50-200 mg/d repeated doses in healthy women ('dose-related pituitary and gonadal suppression'); the 2018 Orilissa label 12.2 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/210450s000lbl.pdf) states the Phase 3 result: 'dose-dependent reduction in median estradiol concentrations to approximately 42 pg/mL for 150 mg once daily regimen and 12 pg/mL for the 200 mg twice daily regimen.' No source found that derives or checks a human exposure target from the macaque (or from the knock-in mouse, where relugolix needed 100 mg/kg BID, Nakata 2014). Kim 2015 (10.1016/j.lfs.2015.08.016) reports elagolix 'suppressed serum LH levels only' in intact female monkeys, a model claim at odds with the E2 suppression seen in women, but that paper makes no patient comparison, so it does not change the status.

efficacy.model: Castrated cynomolgus macaque (LH suppression as efficacy surrogate)
efficacy.note: No endometriosis disease model: the macaque LH readout alone carried elagolix into the clinic for endometriosis.
efficacy.short: No disease model; macaque LH as surrogate
efficacy.quote: These efforts led to the identification of 10b as a clinical compound for the treatment of endometriosis.

efficacy.note: Linzagolix shrank rat cysts at >=50 mg/kg, published after its phase 3s; no source compares rat lesion regression with patient pain response.
efficacy.short: Rat lesion regression never compared to patients
efficacy.quote: Linzagolix significantly decreased cyst volumes compared with the control group at doses of 50 mg/kg or more.
efficacy.reason: Rat lesions never compared with patient pain
efficacy.judgement: Second untested entry added because the model changed (a disease model appeared), not the status. Abstract only (Wiley 403). model_first_use_year 2015 = Kim 2015 (10.1016/j.lfs.2015.08.016), SKI2670, a class proxy never approved, first put an oral GnRH antagonist in a rat endometriosis model. Wang 2026 (10.3791/74321) dosed elagolix 100 mg/kg in a rat autotransplant model (lesion volume -86.7%) and calls it 'consistent with the known mechanism of Elagolix, although pain-related and behavioral outcomes were not evaluated': a retrospective validation against an approved drug, with the patient endpoint (pain) unmeasured and the comparison stated to mechanism, not to patient results, so not scored as 'same'. Relugolix's efficacy surrogate was uterine weight 'to ovariectomized levels' in human-GnRHR knock-in mice (Nakata 2014). Patient side: Taylor 2017 NEJM (10.1056/NEJMoa1700089), dysmenorrhea response 46.4%/75.8% vs 19.6% placebo (EM-I); NCT01620528 results first posted 2018-09-18, NCT01931670 2018-09-07. No primate (baboon/rhesus) endometriosis study of any oral GnRH antagonist found.

safety.model: Rat and mouse toxicology (GnRHR-inactive species) plus monkey
safety.note: Rodent tox is blind to on-target hypo-oestrogenic harm; patients showed dose-dependent BMD loss and ALT rises; no animal-patient comparison found.
safety.short: Rodent tox blind; BMD, ALT harms in patients
safety.quote: because elagolix has low affinity for the GnRH receptor in the rat ... these data have low relevance to humans.
safety.reason: FDA review unread; no comparison found
safety.judgement: Quote is label 13.1 with the bracketed cross-reference '[see Use in Specific Populations (8.1)]' and the fertility clause elided to fit 40 words. Label 5.1: 'ORILISSA causes a dose-dependent decrease in bone mineral density (BMD)'; 5.4: 'dose-dependent elevations of serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) at least 3 times the upper limit'; 13.1 rat liver/thyroid tumours called 'species-specific and of negligible relevance'. BMD loss was anticipated from the GnRH-agonist class in humans, not from an animal model. The FDA multidiscipline review (210450Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf, >10 MB) exists but could not be read in budget; it would show whether monkey toxicology flagged bone or liver and could move this cell to 'same' or 'contra'. registry_date is Elaris EM-II (NCT01931670) results first posted 2018-09-07; EM-I (NCT01620528) 2018-09-18. model_first_use_year null: tox study years not published.
